title: CapturedIntent
description: Capture record for the Gemini prediction market voice assistant. An intent is a record of what the user asked for, stored for later approval. It is never an order: capturing sends nothing to Gemini and `status` is always `captured`. Orders are prediction contracts only: place_order, cancel_order and order_status intents always have venue gemini_prediction. market_query intents and venue gemini_spot are legacy: earlier revisions and the legacy test mode wrote them, the live application does not. The backend mints `id` and `created_at`; every other field comes from a validated tool call (see contracts/tools.json and contracts/api.yaml). Contract revision 3.0.0.

id.description: Backend-minted UUID v4 of this intent. Also usable as the `order_id` of a later cancel_order or order_status intent that refers to this capture.

session_id.description: Voice session that produced the intent. Minted by POST /voice/signed-url. The full timestamped transcript of the session is stored under the same session_id. An identifier, not a credential.

created_at.description: Backend clock, ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 in UTC with a trailing Z, for example 2026-11-18T23:59:01.123Z.

intent.description: place_order and cancel_order are written only by the capture handlers after confirmation enforcement. order_status and market_query are written as an audit record by the simulated query handlers.

venue.description: gemini_prediction for every place_order, cancel_order and order_status intent. gemini_spot appears only on legacy market_query rows. Never null.

instrument.description: place_order: the prediction contract's symbol exactly as search_markets returned it (events[].contracts[].symbol). cancel_order and order_status: the contract symbol when known, otherwise the empty string (order identified by reference only). market_query (legacy): the resolved instrument or the first 64 characters of the search text.

side.description: yes or no for a place_order, meaning buy contracts of that outcome, and for an order_status side filter. buy and sell remain in the enum for schema stability and are not used by any intent since 2.0.0. Null when the intent has no side.

quantity.description: Whole number of contracts, at least 1. Null unless intent is place_order.

limit_price.description: Limit price in US dollars per contract as a decimal number from 0.01 to 0.99 in 0.01 steps (62 cents is stored as 0.62). It is an outcome price, never a price of the underlying asset. Null unless intent is place_order. Only limit orders are captured.

order_id.description: Reference to the order a cancel or status request is about. Either the `id` of a place_order intent captured in the same session, or a reference the user spoke aloud, stored in normalized form (upper case, alphanumerics only). Never invented by the agent. Null for place_order and market_query.

confirmed_by_user.description: True only when the backend verified, against the stored session transcript, an agent readback of these exact terms immediately followed by an explicit spoken yes. Always true for place_order and cancel_order, always false for order_status and market_query.

utterance.description: Raw transcript of the user's own words that stated the request, verbatim from speech recognition, without paraphrase or correction. For place_order and cancel_order it is verified as a contiguous part of the user transcript. For order_status and market_query, when the supplied text is not found in the transcript, it is the latest non-empty user transcript entry cut to 2000 characters. It is never model-written or invented text; the full raw speech is kept in the session transcript.

status.description: Phase 1 has a single status. Captured means recorded and prepared for later approval. It never means submitted, open, filled or cancelled on Gemini.

examples.utterance: five yes contracts on bitcoin above one fifty k at eighteen cents
ten yes contracts on the fed cut at sixty two cents
what's the status of order a b one two three four five
are there any markets on a fed rate cut
